## In plain English
Six hook refusals on 2026-11-20 blocked correct work. This arc takes the three that hit every agent: the commit gate refuses commits into other repositories and refuses commands that hold no commit at all; the Write gate judges a file in a plain folder outside every checkout (the folder that holds this repository's linked worktrees) against the primary checkout's session ritual; and the kill-switch guard refuses read-only commands and plain data writes that only name the flag file.

The recommended fix narrows each gate in place. The commit gate stops judging a commit that lands in a different, non-Directive repository, and stops treating a variable in a command that never says "commit" as a hidden commit. The outside-every-checkout class (#6376) also takes the folders that hold this repository's worktrees. The kill-switch guard counts a few more programs as plain reads and treats a quoted heredoc written to a scratch file as data. Each fix must keep its protection: no commit into the wrong repository, no write into a foreign or primary checkout without the ritual, and no plant of the kill-switch flag.

## Operator decisions (Scott, relayed by the coordinator, 2026-11-20; recorded as constraints)
- Goal: fewer false refusals, ready for the next build. Take evidence items 1, 2 and 6 first: the false positives that hit every agent.
- Each loosening must keep the real protection: no commit to the wrong repository, no write into a foreign or primary checkout without the ritual, and no kill-switch plant.
- Own the gate-logic fixes; defer polfer-owned parts explicitly.
- If the work is more than one reviewable PR, propose a split into child issues.
- Spend: one Codex critic plus a pain audit, critic-post cap 3, one recut.

## Pains
- P1 — The commit gate refuses commands that cannot commit in this repository. A commit named into a different repository (`git -C <abs> commit …` or `cd <abs> && git commit …`) is refused `foreign-repository-deny`, although this repository's story scope does not govern another repository and the gate's own refusal text recommends that form. A call with no commit at all is refused as an unresolvable commit target when a command word holds a variable: a bash array-element assignment such as `M[$k]=v` at the start of a command, a variable program such as `$D verify:x`, or a PowerShell `$env:X = "1"` assignment.
- P2 — A direct Write to a path outside every checkout, but outside the OS temp and home directories, is judged against the payload root's occupancy and session ritual and refused when that ritual is stale. Example: `C:/Repos/deft/wt/notes.md`, in the plain folder that holds this repository's linked worktrees. The #6376 class does not take it: its positive location is temp or home only, and its name rule drops any path with a `deft` or `directive` component anywhere above the target.
- P3 — The kill-switch mention rule (#6681) refuses read-only and data-only commands that name the flag file: a read piped into `cut`, `sort` or `sed -n`, a `git grep`, and a quoted heredoc whose text is written as data to a scratch file. Agents working on any issue about the kill switch hit this on ordinary reads and on writing comment bodies.

## Out of scope (named, not pains)
- Evidence item 3 (a Write to the gitignored `.claude/settings.local.json` in the primary, refused on a stale ritual): not loosened. It is a write into the primary checkout, which the operator's protection keeps under the ritual, and the file is host hook and permission configuration. Recovery stays the printed rearm command.
- Evidence item 4 (a coordinator memory-file Write under the host's dot-folder in the home directory, refused after HEAD moved): the target is in a configuration area, which #6376 keeps out of its class on purpose. The HEAD-move staleness is a possible ritual regression, already reported on #5966 (comment 7046652107). Left to #5966.
- Evidence item 5 (a `session:start` lease in an arc worktree blocks the Codex critic launch with `live-stranger-lease`): dest placement and occupancy (`packages/core/src/design-critique/arc-dest.ts`, `packages/core/src/swarm/dest-place.ts`), a different mechanism from the three gates here. Workaround in use: `session:start --read-only` takes no lease (this arc's dest has none). Proposed below as its own child issue.
- polfer-owned surfaces (per `docs/installer-refactor-ovpr/LLM-CONTEXT.md` section 5): no change to deposited hook files, the `.mjs` outers, `.githooks` helpers, the AC9.12 entry guard for the disable flag, or hook-dispatch root matching (`packages/runtime/src/hook-dispatch.ts`). None of P1-P3 needs one; all three gates are decision logic in `packages/core/src`.
- A bare `git commit` whose shell cwd differs from the payload root (the #6291 limit), the four bypass forms of #6292, and protected-store reads (#6276).

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- R1. Commit gate.
  - R1.1 Foreign repository. When a named commit target is admitted as `foreign-repository` (both common dirs were read and differ) and the target's toplevel is not a Directive project (no `.deft` entry, no `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json`, no `vbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.vbrief.json`), the commit gate returns no decision. A foreign Directive project, including a separate clone of this repository, keeps today's refusal, with text that says to commit from a session in that project. `unproven-identity`, a missing path, a path outside every checkout and same-repository targets are unchanged, and every commit in one call must still name the same target.
  - R1.2 A variable needs a commit word. A variable command word and a `-c`, `env -S` or `eval` string that holds a variable raise the commit signal only when the call's command text, with quoted heredoc bodies removed, contains `commit` in any word, in any case. A variable git subcommand (`git $SUB`) stays a signal, and grouped, wrapped and literal `-c` commits are unchanged.
  - R1.3 Bash array-element assignments (`NAME[subscript]=value`, `NAME[subscript]+=value`) are read as assignments, like `ENV_ASSIGNMENT`, when the word holds no `$(` and no backtick.
- R2. Outside-every-checkout class (#6376).
  - R2.1 A third positive location: inside a worktree container, the parent folder of any worktree that `git worktree list --porcelain` lists for the payload repository (the main worktree included), compared in physical form. A container that is a filesystem or drive root is ignored, and a failed listing adds none.
  - R2.2 For a path that is in a container and not inside temp or home, the `deft`/`directive` component rule reads only the components below that container. Every other rule is unchanged and reads the whole typed and physical paths: the `.git` component rule, configuration areas, environment-named paths, PATH directories, the runtime package, the `.git`/`.deft` ancestor walk, the Git lookup, outside the payload root, and the doubt rules.
  - R2.3 Temp and home keep today's rules exactly. The combining rule, the gates that run and the decision code are unchanged.
- R3. Kill-switch mention rule.
  - R3.1 Plain reads gain `cut`, `tr`, `nl`, `jq`; `sort` unless it has `-o`, `--output` or `--compress-program`; `git grep` unless a word is a short option cluster holding `o` or starts with `--open-files-in-pager` (the text is lowercased, so `-O` fails closed); and `sed` only when every option is one of `-n`, `--quiet`, `--silent`, `-e`, `--expression`, `-r`, `-z`, `-u`, `-s`, and every script is a line-range print (`N`, `N,M`, `$` and `N,$`, each followed by `p`).
  - R3.2 Quoted heredoc data. In the mention test, the body of a quoted-delimiter heredoc is not a mention when its command is `cat` writing it through a `>` or `>>` redirect, or `tee` writing it to its operands, the destinations do not mention the flag, the heredoc command is not piped, and every other segment of the call is a plain read. An unquoted heredoc body (which the shell expands) is read as today. `decideShellWriteReissue` still checks every recognized shell write dest for the flag basename.
  - R3.3 `sed -i` and every other shell write whose command text names the flag stay refused. The deny text gains one sentence: to edit a scratch file that names the flag, use the Edit or Write tool, which checks only the target's name.
- R4. Docs. `content/docs/hook-root-admission.md` (commit-target admission for a foreign repository, the R1.2 signal condition, the worktree container location) and `content/docs/deft-directive-disable.md` (the plain reads and the heredoc data rule).
- R5. Tests beside each changed file, one per case in R1-R3, including each refusal that must stay: a commit into a foreign Directive project or a separate clone, `$GIT commit -m x`, `git $SUB`, a write under `.deft-scratch` or an environment-named path in a container, a container that is a drive root, `sort -o`, `git grep -O`, `sed -n 'w f'`, `sed -i`, a heredoc piped into `sh`, a heredoc whose call also runs `xargs touch`, and a `cat >` whose destination is the flag.
- R6. Split. Three children, one PR each, in priority order: A = R1 (commit gate), B = R2 (write class), C = R3 (mention rule). Each touches one or two source files and one doc. A fourth child, D, carries evidence item 5 (dest lease) as a symptom-only issue for a later arc. No new verb, flag, policy field or stored file.

1. R1.1: does returning no decision for a commit into a non-Directive foreign repository keep "no commit to the wrong repository"? Is the Directive-project marker test sound, and does it keep a separate clone of this repository refused? Should a foreign Directive project instead be judged at its own root?
2. R1.2: does the commit-word condition reopen any form that #6362 closed, beyond splitting the word `commit` across variables (a guardrail, not a boundary, per the doc)? Is the scanned text right?
3. R1.3: can an array-element assignment hide a commit once `$(` and backticks are excluded (for example arithmetic in the subscript)?
4. R2: is the worktree container a sound positive location? 6. R3.3: is it true at the pin that the Edit and Write tools check only the target's basename, so the routing advice is correct?

A variable git subcommand (`git $SUB`), a grouped commit, a wrapped commit and a commit in a literal `-c` string stay signals.
